d026.t: The Spirit Nucleus at the Center
msg: The last section of Paper 12 deals with personal realities, explaining which aspects of reality science, philosophy, and religion each address. This passage concisely sketches the structure of human existence. Mortal man has a spirit nucleus. The mind is a personal-energy system existing around a divine spirit nucleus and functioning in a material environment. And such a living relationship of personal mind and spirit constitutes the universe potential of eternal personality.

The spirit nucleus spoken of here is the Thought Adjuster who indwells us. Just as electrons move around the nucleus of an atom, our minds are active around this divine center. At the deepest center of our being is not our own self but the Father's spirit. When we understand this structure, we come to know who we are and where we ought to place our center. A healthy personality is one in which the mind moves in orderly fashion around the spirit nucleus. The deeper this relationship between Adjuster and mind grows, the more stable the personality becomes and the more certain the possibility of eternal survival.

The text then adds a solemn warning: real trouble, lasting disappointment, serious defeat, or inescapable death can come only after self-concepts presume fully to displace the governing power of the central spirit nucleus, thereby disrupting the cosmic scheme of personality identity. In other words, the deepest misfortune that befalls us comes not from outward events but from the overturning of our inner center. When the self tries to take the place of the spirit, the order of personality collapses. The spirit nucleus never oppresses us; rather, it leads our personality to become most free and whole.

This insight lets us understand much of the pain in our lives anew. We think that failure or loss itself is the greatest misfortune. But for one who keeps the spirit nucleus at the center, failure becomes learning and loss becomes an occasion for growth. Conversely, for one who puts the self at the center, even a small setback becomes an unbearable defeat. The question is less what happens than what stands at the center of my life. When Jesus told us to deny ourselves, he meant just this restoration of the center (see Paper 140). One whose center stands firm is like a ship that does not lose its bearings even in a storm.

The temptation for self-concepts to take the place of the spirit is very subtle. It shows itself as the insistence that things go my way, the certainty that I am right, the craving to be recognized. The self is not bad in itself. The self is a necessary part of the functioning of personality. But trouble arises when the self tries to become the center. The self is healthy when it serves the spirit and sick when it pushes the spirit aside. We need to examine the center of our hearts every day. When we lay down the self with a humble heart, the true self comes alive.

I invite you today to look quietly at what stands at the center of your heart. If your own will and your own pride are seated there, give that place back to the Father's spirit. When the mind is set in order around the spirit nucleus, we gain a peace that does not collapse in any circumstance. And in that living relationship our personality grows toward eternal existence.
d026.pr: Today, when the urge to insist on your own way arises, pause and pray, asking first for the Father's will rather than your own.

msg: Paper 13 describes the sacred spheres that circle Paradise, and in its first section it introduces the seven sacred worlds of the Father. The first of these is Divinington. This passage says that Divinington is, in a unique sense, the “⟦Q 13:1.4⟧bosom of the Father,⟦/Q⟧” the personal-communion sphere of the Universal Father, and that thereon is a special manifestation of his divinity. And it reveals that Divinington is the Paradise rendezvous of the Thought Adjusters.

This fact holds deep meaning for us. The Adjuster now indwelling our minds is a being who came from the very bosom of the Father. The Adjuster set out from Divinington to come to us, and even while with us he never loses his connection with the Father. The spirit within us is linked to the holiest place in the universe, the place where the Father personally communes. Our inner life thus touches the deepest center of the universe. The Adjuster, a pure fragment of the Father, left that bosom and came to us in order to bring us to the Father. That journey itself tells how great the Father's love is.

The text says that Divinington is the home not only of the Adjusters but of numerous other entities, personalities, and beings taking origin in the Universal Father. And it adds that only the Father fragments and those beings of direct and exclusive origin in the Universal Father fraternize and function on this abode. Divinington is the home of the beings to whom the Father alone has given origin. Among its secrets is the secret of the bestowal and indwelling of the Adjusters (see Paper 107). The Adjuster renews the Father's love within us day by day.

The phrase “⟦Q 13:1.4⟧bosom of the Father⟦/Q⟧” has a warm resonance. The bosom is the place of the closest love, the place of being held and protected. That the Adjuster within us came from the Father's bosom means that we live with the Father's closest love abiding within us. When we are lonely and weary, we need not go far to find the Father's bosom. To return within and become conscious of the Adjuster's presence is to rest in the Father's embrace. The Father's bosom is not only in the distant heavens but also within our hearts, where his spirit dwells. This assures us that wherever we are, we are never orphans.

This truth makes our attitude toward the Adjuster reverent. The One in our minds is not merely the voice of conscience but a divine being who came down from the Father's bosom. Our minds, which host him, are a holy sanctuary. The thoughts and feelings we harbor can either cleanse that sanctuary or cloud it. Tending our minds so that the Adjuster can work at ease is the most beautiful hospitality we can offer. That hospitality consists of honest thoughts, loving feelings, and sincere prayers.

I invite you today to take a quiet moment to meditate on the fact that the Adjuster within you came from the bosom of the Father. And give him thanks. We live on a small planet on the edge of the universe, yet within us dwells One who came from the holiest center of the universe. Whoever remembers this never leaves the Father's bosom, wherever he may be.
d027.pr: Today, close your eyes for a moment, remember that the Adjuster within you came from the bosom of the Father, and give thanks.

d028.t: At the Right Hand of the Father
msg: The second section of Paper 13 explains the relation of ascenders to the sacred worlds of the Father. This passage tells us both the privileges the ascending mortal will one day enjoy and their limits. Eventually we will have full access to Ascendington and relative access to the other spheres of the Father except Divinington. Yet even after we have become finaliters, we will not be allowed to visit all sectors of such worlds.

Ascendington is the world known as the bosom of the ascending souls. It is a sacred home that ascending mortals like us will one day freely enter and leave. The Father has prepared a special world for ascenders, and there we will understand more deeply the meaning of our own ascension experience. It is a great comfort that, in the order of the universe, an honorable place has been prepared even for evolutionary creatures like us (see Paper 14). At every stage of ascension we are allowed to draw near to more as we are made ready, and that gradual opening is itself the Father's careful consideration.

The text says that we will never be permitted to land on the shores of Divinington, the bosom of the Father. And it adds that never throughout all eternity will there arise any necessity for our presence on the world of the Thought Adjusters. Why is this so? Because when we fuse with the Adjuster, that divine being becomes one with us, and the Father's bosom will already be within us without our going to Divinington. The Father's spirit becomes so fully one with us that there is no need to go there. So minutely has the Father planned and prepared our eternal future.

Instead, the text gives a beautiful promise: we shall surely stand repeatedly at the “⟦Q 13:2.7⟧right hand of the Father.⟦/Q⟧” The right hand is the place of trust, glory, and intimacy. A being who began in the clay at last standing at the right hand of the Father: this is the glorious culmination of the ascension career. And that place is given not once but again and again. The Father delights to keep his children beside him. This promise reveals not a distance between the Father and us but rather the deepest oneness. It is not that we go in search of his bosom; it is that his bosom comes into us and abides there forever.

This passage also teaches us respect for the divine order. Being satisfied only when we know everything and can go everywhere is an immature attitude. In the universe there are places open to us and places closed, and the distinction is not discrimination but wise order. Being grateful for what is granted to us and respecting what is not granted is the mark of a mature spirit. This humility is a virtue needed here on earth as well. That humility becomes a ladder leading us higher.

I invite you today to picture the day when you will stand at the right hand of the Father. Our present life, as we walk toward that day, is a time of preparing for that glory. The more we co-operate with the Adjuster and do the Father's will, the nearer that place of glory comes. One who lives with the Father's bosom abiding within, without needing to go to Divinington, is the very one who will one day stand at the Father's right hand.
d028.pr: Spend today with a heart that is grateful for what is granted to you and humbly accepts what is not.

msg: Paper 14 describes the central universe of Havona, and in its fifth section it deals with life in Havona. As it opens that description, this passage shows us our whole ascension career at a glance. On Urantia we pass through a short and intense test during our initial life of material existence. Rising through the mansion worlds and the system, constellation, and local universe, we traverse the morontia phases of ascension; on the training worlds of the superuniverse we pass through the true spirit stages and are prepared for eventual transit to Havona.

Within this short passage is contained the map of our eternal journey. Life on this earth is only the first stage of that long journey. Death is not an end but a door to the next stage. On the mansion worlds we learn what we failed to learn here; in the local universe we grow as morontia beings; in the superuniverse we are refined as spirit beings. And at last, on the seven circuits of Havona, our attainment becomes intellectual, spiritual, and experiential (see Paper 47). One who keeps this map in mind views present difficulties from the perspective of eternity and can tell what passes from what endures.

Yet the revelator calls life on this earth a short and intense test. Compared with eternity, our lifetime is short indeed. But that short time is by no means light; on the contrary, it is intense. Holding fast to God by faith in a material body, with an animal nature, in an uncertain environment, is a unique experience that can never be repeated at any later stage. Faith that believes without seeing is a precious test possible only on this earth. Every part of this process has been designed by the Father's love.

This perspective lets us see our difficulties anew. Life on this earth is hard not because we have been abandoned but because it is the place of an intense test. Tests are given not to break us but to temper us. The small victories won by faith on this earth become the foundation that upholds our whole eternal career. The courage, patience, and trust cultivated amid difficulty are treasures that can be obtained nowhere else. One day we will look back on our short time on this earth and realize how precious were the steps we took then in faith. It is said that the ascenders on the mansion worlds, too, regard their experience on the material world as a precious asset.

The text says that there is a definite task to be achieved on each of the worlds of each of the Havona circuits. Our ascension career is not aimless wandering but a course of education with clear goals and tasks. It is the same on this earth. There is something we must learn right here and now. Being faithful to the task given today, neither hurrying nor putting it off, is the way to go faithfully through the eternal curriculum. Day upon day, faithfully built up in this way, becomes the solid foundation of an eternal career.

I invite you today to accept the difficulties of your life as part of a short and intense test. And resolve to pass that test by faith. Our time on this earth is short, but the decisions made in that time endure forever. The long road from the mansion worlds to Havona lies before us, and its first step is the step of faith we take here and now.
d029.pr: Today, regard one difficulty you face as an intense test for the eternal journey, and meet it with faith.

msg: The last section of Paper 14 explains the purposes of the central universe of Havona, setting out in turn what it means to the Father, the Son, the Spirit, the Supreme Being, and various orders of beings. This passage tells what Havona means to ascending mortals. These worlds provide the stimulus of all human impulses towards the attainment of true spirit values on the highest conceivable reality levels. Havona is the pre-Paradise training goal of every ascending mortal.

In our hearts there is a longing for higher things: the desire to become truer, more beautiful, and more good. Where does this longing come from? The text says that the perfect universe of Havona provides the stimulus of all these human impulses. Because a pattern of perfection actually exists, the ideals within us point not toward vague dreams but toward real goals. Havona is the actual realization of the highest ideals we cherish. The high longings within us, then, are not empty fancies but a pull toward reality.

The text goes on to say that in Havona mortals attain pre-Paradise Deity, the Supreme Being. The Supreme Being is God evolving in time and space, and our experience and growth together contribute to his actualization (see Paper 117). Passing through the circuits of Havona, we come to know the Supreme Being experientially, and in our relationship with him we realize that our own experience has universe significance. Our small growth is never a merely private matter. The perfection of Havona exists not to intimidate us but to beckon us.

The last sentence of this passage defines Havona in this way: Havona stands before every will creature as the portal to Paradise and God attainment. A portal is a door that exists to be passed through. Havona is in itself a beautiful and perfect universe, but for ascenders it is the door of final preparation for reaching the Father. Beyond that door we shall at last behold the Universal Father. The whole ascension career moves toward this portal. In Havona we will not be students studying alone but members of a community learning and growing together with countless ascenders and the Havona natives.

This teaching encourages our idealism. The world often dismisses ideals as unrealistic and tells us to make our peace with reality. But The Urantia Book teaches that perfection actually exists and that we are destined to reach it. To cherish high ideals, therefore, is not to turn away from reality but to look upon the deepest reality. Ideals are the inner compass that leads us to Havona and to the Father. A life that has lost its ideals has lost its direction, but a life that cherishes ideals gains new strength day by day.

I invite you today to call to mind the highest ideal in your heart. And remember that this ideal is actually realized in the perfection of Havona. When you carry out one small thing you can do today toward that ideal, you are already on the road to the portal. Havona is far away, but the longing for it transforms us here and now.
d030.pr: Write down the highest ideal you hold, and do one small thing today that moves you toward it.

msg: Paper 15 explains the structure and administration of the seven superuniverses. The vast organization reaching from systems and constellations to local universes, minor sectors, and major sectors is the subject of this paper. Yet before any of that explanation, the paper opens with a remarkable sentence: as far as the Universal Father is concerned, as a Father, the universes are virtually nonexistent; he deals with personalities; he is the Father of personalities. Not even the vast organization of the universe stands at the center of the Father's concern; his concern is always with personality.

This sentence turns our view of the universe upside down. We are easily overwhelmed by the size of a universe made up of hundreds of billions of stars and trillions of planets, and feel that a single person within it is smaller than a speck of dust. But from the Father's point of view, that immense material universe is rather a mere backdrop. What the Father deals with is not stars and galaxies but children who possess personality. The personality of a single person living on the smallest planet is nearer to the Father than countless stars. His concern lies not in numbers or scale but in personalities who can love and be loved.

The text distinguishes how each person of Deity is related to the universes. For the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit, as creator partners, the universes are localized and individual under the joint rule of the Creator Sons and the Creative Spirits. For the Paradise Trinity, outside Havona there are the seven superuniverses. And the Seven Master Spirits, with Paradise as the hub and their own influence as the spokes, constitute the vast creation one gigantic wheel. The administration and order of the universe are entrusted to them, while the Father, as the Father of personalities, relates directly to his children (see Paper 5). When we pray, we are not sending up a faint signal from some corner of a vast universe; we are speaking directly to a Father who knows us well.

This truth shows us how direct our way to the Father is. The Father is not one who merely receives reports at the top of a vast bureaucracy. He is directly connected with every personality through the personality circuit, and he dwells directly in our minds through the Adjuster. However complex the administration of the universe may be, the relationship between the Father and his child is simple and direct. We can speak to the Father without any intermediary, and the Father hears us.

This teaching also tells us what we ought to value most. If the Father puts personality at the center, we too must put people at the center. We are easily so absorbed in work, results, things, and systems that we neglect people. But what endures forever is not buildings or achievements but personalities and the love between them. Doing our work well matters, but serving people and giving them life through that work matters more.

I invite you today to look at the world through the Father's eyes. Value the faces of the people you meet more than the list of things you must do. Give thanks that in this vast universe the Father deals with you as a person, and treat the people beside you, too, with care as persons. As we do so, we grow to resemble the heart of the One who is the Father of personalities.
d031.pr: Today, attend to the hearts of the people you work with before the results of the work, and show one person sincere interest.

d032.t: Living in a Universe of Mercy
msg: The final section of Paper 15 deals with the purpose of the seven superuniverses and introduces the character of Orvonton, the seventh superuniverse, to which we belong. This paragraph beautifully sums up what Orvonton is known for. Orvonton “⟦Q 15:14.2⟧is known chiefly because of its tremendous and lavish bestowal of merciful ministry to the mortals of the realms.⟦/Q⟧” It is renowned “⟦Q 15:14.2⟧for the manner in which justice prevails as tempered by mercy and power rules as conditioned by patience.⟦/Q⟧”

How blessed is the universe in which we live! Each of the seven superuniverses has its own purpose and character, and our Orvonton is a universe of mercy. Here justice is not carried out coldly but is softened by mercy; power is not wielded in haste but is tempered by patience. Our own planet, Urantia, which has passed through rebellion and confusion, is cared for within this very order of mercy. The opportunities and the seasons of recovery we now enjoy are all the fruit of that mercy. It is given not because we deserve it, but because such is the very nature of the Father’s love. It is because we live in this universe of mercy that we can rise again from the places where we have failed.

The passage tells us that in Orvonton “⟦Q 15:14.2⟧the sacrifices of time are freely made to secure the stabilization of eternity.⟦/Q⟧” The rulers of the universe look beyond immediate order to eternal outcomes, and they wait, and wait again. Even toward sin and rebellion they do not rush to judgment; they allow time so that every creature may have ample opportunity to turn back. The long delay in adjudicating the Lucifer rebellion is one expression of this patience (see Paper 54). In that waiting lies a heart that longs to save even one more soul. The very fact that a world wounded by rebellion, as ours has been, is still on the road to recovery is itself evidence of this patience. God’s time is far wider and deeper than our impatience.

The paragraph closes with the words “⟦Q 15:14.2⟧Orvonton is a universe demonstration of love and mercy.⟦/Q⟧” A demonstration is a showing forth. Orvonton is showing the whole universe that love and mercy truly work as the principles by which a universe is governed. And at the summit of that demonstration stands Michael’s bestowal on Urantia. The mercy, patience, and forgiveness that Jesus revealed on this earth are the clearest disclosure of the character of Orvonton.

We who live in a universe of mercy ought surely to become merciful people. If we do not extend to our neighbors the mercy we ourselves have received, we are going against the very spirit of the universe we inhabit. To establish justice yet soften it with mercy, to use power yet temper it with patience, and to look for eternal fruit rather than immediate results: this is the life worthy of a citizen of Orvonton. At home, at work, and in society, we can become small demonstrations of that spirit. Mercy is not weakness; it is the expression of the most mature strength. Only those who have learned to govern themselves can show true mercy to others.

Today, when you feel the urge to judge someone, remember the spirit of Orvonton. As the rulers of the universe deal with us, so let us also refrain from haste, be willing to wait, and choose mercy before severity. Our small acts of patience and forgiveness, gathered together, become evidence that the universe we live in is truly a universe of love and mercy.
d032.pr: Today, when faced with someone’s wrongdoing, hold back from judging at once; wait a day and prepare a merciful response.

msg: Every day we look at things, weigh right and wrong, and open our hearts toward something higher. Today’s passage teaches that these three activities are not habits that arose by chance; they are the three insights of the cosmic mind, planted within us through the local universe mind bestowals. “⟦Q 16:6.10⟧Matter-energy is recognized by the mathematical logic of the senses; mind-reason intuitively knows its moral duty; spirit-faith (worship) is the religion of the reality of spiritual experience.⟦/Q⟧” Science, philosophy, and religion are not rival contenders but three responses to reality set together within one personality.

Paper 16 calls these three insights causation, duty, and worship (see 16:6.6–6.8). They are a priori assumptions, given to us before anything is learned. That is why we know that the world is real, that we ought to do good, and that God exists, even before we argue for any of it. Because of these intuitions, man is able “⟦Q 16:6.10⟧to function as a rational and self-conscious personality,⟦/Q⟧” and can lay hold of things, meanings, and values as realities. The universe has opened our minds by just such “⟦Q 16:6.10⟧a cosmic technique of self-revelation.⟦/Q⟧”

What the passage carefully warns against is imbalance. The three factors “⟦Q 16:6.10⟧may be unified and co-ordinated in personality development, or they may become disproportionate and virtually unrelated in their respective functions.⟦/Q⟧” Those who merely pile up facts may know a great deal and yet easily lose the meaning of life; those who delight only in abstract speculation become trapped in argument; and those who pursue only religious feeling are prone to blindness, turning their backs on facts. The Urantia Book says again and again that personality attains balance only when science and religion are linked by a wise philosophy (see Paper 103).

When the three insights are bound together, they produce, in the words of the passage, “⟦Q 16:6.10⟧a strong character.⟦/Q⟧” When the scientific attitude that deals honestly with facts, the moral philosophy that searches deeply into meanings, and the religious experience of living fellowship with God all mesh together, we become people who do not fear facts, do not evade duty, and do not neglect worship. Such people do not abandon reason for the sake of faith, nor lose faith for the sake of reason. Within them, knowledge, goodness, and adoration guard one another.

This teaching is especially precious in today’s culture. Many people think that to believe in science one must give up religion, and that to keep religion one must be wary of science. But according to this passage, the capacity to know facts, the capacity to know duty, and the capacity to worship God are siblings born of the same cosmic mind. Cut one away, and the other two grow weaker. Faith that ignores facts tends to become superstition, knowledge that has lost its values becomes a dangerous power, and morality without worship easily hardens into dry law. The balanced person, therefore, is honest in the laboratory, follows conscience in daily life, and in quiet hours communes with God.

Let us look at this day with these three eyes: seeing honestly what has happened, just as it is; asking what is the right thing I ought to do in the face of it; and lifting it all up to the Universal Father in thanksgiving. As we practice holding even a small decision up to the light of fact, duty, and worship together, our personality becomes, little by little, more unified. And just such a unified personality becomes the soil of mind in which the Thought Adjuster can work most freely.
d033.pr: Before one decision today, ask three questions: What are the facts? What is the right thing to do? What shall I offer up to God?

msg: Today’s passage makes it very clear where brotherhood comes from: “⟦Q 16:9.14⟧You become conscious of man as your creature brother because you are already conscious of God as your Creator Father.⟦/Q⟧” Brotherly love does not begin with social courtesy or emotional closeness. First comes the fact that we are children of the same Father, and then, along the path of reason that recognizes this fact, brotherhood comes into view. “⟦Q 16:9.14⟧Fatherhood is the relationship out of which we reason ourselves into the recognition of brotherhood.⟦/Q⟧”

The passage says this relationship is no vague metaphor but a universe reality, because “⟦Q 16:9.14⟧the Father has himself bestowed personality upon all such beings and has encircuited them within the grasp of the universal personality circuit.⟦/Q⟧” My personality, and the personality of the stranger I will meet today, are equally gifts from the Universal Father. To despise that person, then, is to make light of the One who gave him personality, and to honor that person becomes another way of worshiping the Father.

Just before this paragraph, Paper 16 frankly admits that unselfishness is not natural, and that people are not by nature lovable or social (see 16:9.7). How, then, can we love others? When Jesus revealed God as Father, he at the same time gave a new revelation of man. The deeper our experience of knowing God as Father grows, the deeper grows our vision of our neighbor as a brother. Brotherhood is less a virtue we squeeze out by effort than the fruit borne by knowing the Father.

Finally, the passage gives three reasons for worship: “⟦Q 16:9.14⟧We worship God, first, because he is, then, because he is in us, and last, because we are in him.⟦/Q⟧” These three reasons are like stages in the maturing of faith. At first we stand in awe at the fact that a great Creator exists; next we discover him dwelling within us as the Thought Adjuster; and at last we realize that we ourselves are held within his infinite life. The awareness that we are in him leads on to the awareness that everyone beside us is also in him.

This teaching transforms, at the root, the way we see human relationships. We usually draw close to those who are like us, those who benefit us, and those who like us. But if the ground of brotherhood lies in our common Father, the circle of brotherhood is not drawn by my tastes or my interests. Whatever their race, language, or religion, however different their temperaments and opinions, all are children of the Father, held within the same personality circuit. Jesus’ command to love even our enemies is rooted in this fact. If the Father has not given up on someone, I have no right to cast him out of the place of a brother.

Let us look at the people we meet today in this light. The colleague we do not get along with, the family member who seems bothersome, the stranger we pass on the street: all are brothers and sisters who received their personality from the same Father. When you feel the urge to judge someone, remember that God is in that person too, and that person is in God. When our worship of the Father flows out into service to our brothers, our religion at last becomes a living religion. And in doing so we come to know by experience that worship and service are not two things but one.
d034.pr: Call to mind one person you find difficult today, remember that he too received his personality from the Universal Father, and bless him.

msg: When we think of the record of a life, we usually picture documents, photographs, and résumés. Today’s passage tells us that the universe has formal records too, but that there is a deeper, spiritual record as well. “⟦Q 17:3.6⟧The formal records of the universes are passed up by and through the angelic recorders, but the true spiritual records are assembled by reflectivity and are preserved in the minds of suitable and appropriate personalities belonging to the family of the Infinite Spirit.⟦/Q⟧” The passage calls these “⟦Q 17:3.6⟧the live records in contrast with the formal and dead records of the universe.⟦/Q⟧”

“⟦Q 17:3.5⟧The Reflective Spirits are not merely transmitting agents; they are retentive personalities as well,⟦/Q⟧” and so are their offspring, the seconaphim. “⟦Q 17:3.5⟧Everything of true spiritual value is registered in duplicate.⟦/Q⟧” This shows how highly the universe prizes spiritual values. Material achievements scatter with the passing of time, but spiritual realities, such as deeds done in love, honest decisions for truth, and reverence before beauty, are kept in duplicate so that not one of them is lost.

This teaching is closely linked with the doctrine of survival found throughout The Urantia Book. The true spiritual values in mortal experience are preserved by the Thought Adjuster, and the surviving soul is made of just such values (see Paper 16, section 9, and Paper 112). The universe is not a ledger that stores up our mistakes and failings forever, but a vast memory that holds the spiritual fruits we have borne in living minds. Even a small good deed done where no one sees it never vanishes from the living records of the universe.

What, then, in our lives is worth recording? How much we possessed or how high we rose may appear in the formal records, but these are not at the heart of the living records. What the universe preserves is true spiritual value: the moment we trusted God in the midst of suffering, the moment we turned bitterness into forgiveness, the moment we shared the burden of a neighbor. Such moments may look humble on the outside, yet they become records that shine in eternity.

Here we may reflect deeply on the difference between formal records and living records. A formal record notes precisely what happened and when, but it cannot capture the motive and the depth of love within the deed. A living record, by contrast, is preserved in the mind of a personality, and so it keeps not only the outward form of an act but also the spiritual reality that gave birth to it. The same offering, the same service, carries an entirely different weight in the living records of the universe when the heart behind it differs. The ancient truth that God looks upon the heart is here confirmed as a cosmic fact. We should therefore care more about leaving a true record before God than about records meant to be seen by others.

As we go through this day, let us ask: What, in the work I am doing now, is worthy of being preserved forever? This question rescues us from vanity and hurry and brings us back to the essentials of love, truth, and faithfulness. Every day we are writing something into the living minds of the universe. May that record be filled with spiritual values that please the Father. Even if the world does not remember, the universe remembers. With this faith we can do good gladly even in hidden places, and need not lose heart in service that goes unrecognized.
d035.pr: Before you fall asleep, find one spiritual value in today’s deeds worthy of being preserved forever, and give thanks for it.

msg: Today’s passage is short, but it reveals the starting point of our minds. The adjutant spirits “⟦Q 17:7.1⟧are the sevenfold mind bestowal of a local universe Mother Spirit upon the living creatures⟦/Q⟧” of her creation. “⟦Q 17:7.1⟧This bestowal becomes possible at the time of the Spirit’s elevation to the status of personality prerogatives.⟦/Q⟧” In other words, beneath our capacity to think, to learn, and to choose lies a gift of love from the Mother Spirit of Nebadon. Our minds did not come about by chance; they were given in loving care.

The Urantia Book names these seven adjutant mind-spirits: the spirit of intuition, the spirit of understanding, the spirit of courage, the spirit of knowledge, the spirit of counsel, the spirit of worship, and the spirit of wisdom (see Paper 36, section 5). The first five also function in animal life, but the spirits of worship and wisdom function only in the minds of creatures, such as man, who are able to seek God. When these two begin to operate, an evolving being at last acquires a moral nature and becomes ready to receive a Thought Adjuster.

This teaching is connected with the great family of the Third Source and Center described in Paper 17. From the Infinite Spirit come the Seven Master Spirits; under their influence the Creative Spirit of the local universe carries on her work; and that Creative Spirit in turn ministers to our minds through the adjutant spirits. The river of mind that rises on Paradise passes through many levels and at last flows into the thoughts of each one of us. Even our most ordinary thought touches the farthest reach of that vast ministry of mind.

Knowing this changes how we treat our minds. We no longer use the mind merely as a tool for success; we cultivate it as a sacred vessel for seeking God and learning truth. In the face of fear we can lean on the spirit of courage, in confusion we can seek the spirit of counsel, and before a decision we can ask for the spirit of wisdom. Above all, the spirit of worship reminds us that our minds were made, by their very nature, to open upward.

The ministry of the adjutant spirits goes on unceasingly, even when we are not aware of it. The help of this sevenfold mind permeates every process: the newborn coming to know the world, the child learning to speak, the young person summoning courage before danger, the adult seeking wisdom in counsel with others. The Urantia Book explains that when the races of an evolving world first looked up to the heavens in awe and began to seek God, this too was the work of the spirit of worship. Man’s religious instinct, then, is not an illusion born of ignorance but a longing the universe planted in the mind from the beginning. This assures us that our prayer and worship are never monologues spoken into empty air.

Today, let us remember that our minds are a gift from the Mother Spirit. When our thoughts scatter, let us pause to thank the One who gave us mind, and make a sincere effort to understand the tasks entrusted to us. To respect the mind and use it well is to honor the One who gave it. A mind that co-operates with the ministry of the adjutant spirits grows ever more sensitive to the leading of the Spirit of Truth and the Thought Adjuster. Those who have received the gift of mind are called to walk the path that leads back to its Giver. Each of our thoughts can be a step along that path.
d036.pr: When you meet a difficulty today, pause to pray, asking for whichever you need most now: courage, counsel, or wisdom.

msg: Today’s passage concerns the secret worlds of the Father that lie near Paradise. “⟦Q 18:1.6⟧To beings of even high universe attainment these secret worlds ever remain a test of loyalty.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 18:1.6⟧It is given us fully and personally to know the eternal Gods, freely to know their characters of divinity and perfection, but it is not granted us fully to penetrate all of the personal relations of the Paradise Rulers with all of their creature beings.⟦/Q⟧”

There is a very deep spiritual lesson here. The character of God is open to us, but the personal relationship between God and another being is kept as something belonging to that being and God alone. The Universal Father enters into an individual and unique relationship with every creature. The mystery of that relationship cannot be looked into by anyone else, not even by exalted celestial beings. It is a sign of how personally the Father deals with each of his children.

Why, then, is this a test of loyalty? An attitude that will trust only after knowing everything is not true trust. As the Lucifer rebellion shows, even a being of high station fell into pride when he could not accept the limits of his own understanding (see Paper 53). To believe in God’s goodness and to respect his rule even in the face of what we cannot know: that is cosmic loyalty. Loyalty is revealed not when we hold all the answers, but where we do not know them.

Our daily lives have such secret worlds as well. We cannot fully know why certain things happen to another person, or why God leads someone in a particular way. To judge our neighbor’s spiritual journey rashly, or to think we fully understand the relationship between that person and God, runs contrary to this teaching. Between each soul and God there is a holy intimacy that deserves our respect.

This teaching also instructs us in an attitude of humble intellect. Revelation tells us much, but it does not tell us everything. Even the exalted being who wrote this paper confesses that he can disclose almost nothing about what takes place on the secret worlds of the Father. The high intelligences of the universe honestly acknowledge the realms they cannot know, and they accept those limits not with complaint but with reverence. We, too, need not pretend to have every answer when faced with questions of faith. A heart that can confess “⟦Q 3:6.6⟧I do not know⟦/Q⟧” and still trust is the mark of a mature believer. Mystery does not threaten faith; it is the wide space in which faith grows.

Today, let us practice trusting even when we do not understand everything. Rather than forcing a solution to the unresolved questions in our lives, let us remember the Father’s character and entrust them to him. And let us learn the humility that respects the faith and experience of others and does not presume to measure the relationship between them and God. The loyalty we keep before the unknowable makes us, more and more, trustworthy citizens of the universe. One who can entrust everything without knowing everything can be at peace even before the secrets of Paradise. Loyalty is measured not by the breadth of our understanding but by the depth of our trust.
d037.pr: Call to mind one thing you cannot understand, and pray, entrusting it to the Father in confidence of his goodness.

msg: Today’s passage shows how the universe is governed. “⟦Q 18:3.9⟧The Supreme Being is achieving the sovereignty of the seven superuniverses by experiential service just as a Creator Son experientially earns the sovereignty of his local universe.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 18:3.9⟧But during the present age of the unfinished evolution of the Supreme, the Ancients of Days provide the co-ordinated and perfect administrative overcontrol of the evolving universes of time and space.⟦/Q⟧” And “⟦Q 18:3.9⟧the wisdom of originality and the initiative of individuality characterize all the decrees and rulings of the Ancients of Days.⟦/Q⟧”

This short paragraph holds a remarkable universe principle: even the highest beings do not simply proclaim their sovereignty; they earn it through experience. Michael, the Creator Son of our local universe, became a full sovereign only after living the lives of his own creatures in person through seven bestowals, and the last of those bestowals was the life of Jesus on Urantia (see Paper 120). The Supreme Being, too, is evolving in time and space and building up sovereignty through experience.

Until that process is completed, the Ancients of Days care for the universe with perfection and fairness. Because they reveal the character of the Trinity, their rulings are always righteous. Yet the passage tells us that those rulings are not the mechanical application of rules; they are rendered with original wisdom and individual initiative. Even perfect justice is administered within a living wisdom that considers each situation and each personality.

This teaches us two things for our own lives. First, true authority comes from experience and service. If we hold a place of leadership, whether at home or at work, it is not our position that gives us authority but the experience of having gone through things together and shared the burden. Second, the same is true of our own growth. Spiritual maturity is not conferred by a single declaration; it is gained little by little through the daily experience of doing God’s will.

The story of Michael shows this principle most beautifully. As Creator he already possessed great power, yet in order truly to understand and sympathize with the creatures he had made, he humbled himself to take their form. Living as Jesus on Urantia, he worked as a carpenter, supported a family, and endured misunderstanding, rejection, and even death. Through that experience he became a sovereign who knows our weaknesses firsthand. Before him, then, we need not fear being misunderstood. Sovereignty earned by experience is not the cold authority of command but the warm authority of one who has suffered with us and overcome with us. Here is the very pattern of the leadership we are to follow.

We are beings who share, in a small way, in the evolution of the Supreme Being. The Urantia Book teaches that the spiritual growth we achieve through experience in time contributes to the experiential actualization of the Supreme (see Paper 117). So let us not regard today’s difficulties and lessons as futile. Today’s experience becomes tomorrow’s wisdom, and that wisdom contributes to the growth of the whole universe. Only what is gained by experience truly becomes our own. As Michael came to understand us through experience, let us also become people who understand our neighbors through experience. Today’s small obedience lays the foundation of an eternal sovereignty.
d038.pr: In the place entrusted to you today, before giving any direction, first carry out one act of sharing the work and serving alongside others.

msg: When we want to understand something, we usually ask about its beginning. We tend to think that if we know where it came from and how it arose, we know its essence. Today’s passage points out the limits of this habit. “⟦Q 19:1.5⟧The human mind would ordinarily crave to approach the cosmic philosophy portrayed in these revelations by proceeding from the simple and the finite to the complex and the infinite, from human origins to divine destinies. But that path does not lead to spiritual wisdom.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 19:1.5⟧At best it can only reveal man’s origin; it reveals little or nothing about his divine destiny.⟦/Q⟧”

The passage says that even in the study of biologic evolution, “⟦Q 19:1.6⟧there are grave objections to the exclusive historic approach.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 19:1.6⟧The true perspective of any reality problem — human or divine, terrestrial or cosmic — can be had only by the full and unprejudiced study and correlation of three phases of universe reality: origin, history, and destiny.⟦/Q⟧” This is also how The Urantia Book explains the universe. The revelation begins with the Universal Father on Paradise and proceeds downward, helping us to understand man from above, that is, in the light of his destiny.

Let us apply this teaching to ourselves. People often define themselves by their past. They think that the family they were born into, the wounds they have received, and the failures they have suffered explain who they are. Origin and history do matter, of course. But they alone cannot tell the whole of who I am. I began from an animal origin, yet I am a son of God indwelt by a Thought Adjuster, a being called to see the Father on Paradise. My destiny is the most important part of my identity.

The same holds when we look at others. If we see only a person’s past and present condition, we are quick to judge and to conclude. But that person, too, has a divine destiny. Though he may now seem weak and clumsy, the Father’s spirit working within him is leading him toward perfection. Those who see destiny as well do not easily give up on others. Eyes that see only origins imprison people, but eyes that see destiny raise them up.

The passage says that “⟦Q 19:1.6⟧the proper understanding of these three experiential realities affords the basis for a wise estimate of the current status.⟦/Q⟧” So it is with the situation I face today. When I look together at where it began, what course it has taken, and where it is heading, my present problem appears not as despair but as a stage of growth. If we dwell only on past causes, we easily remain stuck in regret and resentment; but when we look toward destiny, today’s steps take on meaning.

This also gives an important insight into the relationship between science and religion. Evolutionary science has revealed in astonishing detail how man came to be. But it must remain silent on why man exists and where he is going. Conversely, when religion ignores the facts of origin and history, it easily falls into blind credulity. The Urantia Book does not ask us to discard either one. When we hold together the science that uncovers origins and the revelation that illuminates destiny, we come to understand man as a whole. True perspective arises only when knowledge rising from below meets wisdom descending from above.

Today, let us practice looking at ourselves and those around us in the light of destiny. Let us humbly acknowledge where we have come from, but remember more often where we are going. We began in time, but we are beings bound for eternity. Those who remember that destiny do not collapse at small failures; day by day they choose the Father’s will anew and press forward.
d039.pr: Today, call to mind one part of your past that has defined you, and in its place write down the destiny God has given you.

msg: Where does wisdom come from? Today’s passage tells us that “⟦Q 19:2.4⟧wisdom is twofold in origin, being derived from the perfection of divine insight inherent in perfect beings and from the personal experience acquired by evolutionary creatures.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 19:2.4⟧The Perfectors of Wisdom are the divine wisdom of the Paradise perfection of Deity insight,⟦/Q⟧” while the ascendant personalities, “⟦Q 19:2.4⟧the Mighty Messengers, Those without Name and Number, and Those High in Authority, when acting together, are the universe wisdom of experience.⟦/Q⟧”

The most striking point in the passage is the admission that neither kind of being alone can exhaust all possible wisdom. “⟦Q 19:2.4⟧A divine being can have perfection of divine knowledge. An evolutionary mortal can sometime attain perfection of ascendant knowledge.⟦/Q⟧” But perfect knowledge and perfect wisdom are not the same thing. And so, whenever the greatest wisdom is needed in superuniverse administration, the perfectors of the wisdom of divine insight are always associated with those ascendant personalities “⟦Q 19:2.4⟧who have come up to the high responsibilities of superuniverse authority through the experiential tribulations of evolutionary progression.⟦/Q⟧”

Here we see how highly the universe values experience. Even the perfection of Paradise has need of the experience of beings who have grown up through hardship in time. This is a great comfort to us. Our mistakes and trials, our tears and recoveries, are not in vain. They are experiential treasure that will add to the wisdom of the universe forever. To be born an evolutionary mortal is not a defect; it is a place of unique contribution that perfect beings can never fill in our stead.

At the same time, this teaching asks humility of us. Experience alone does not bring wisdom to completion. Experience becomes true wisdom when it meets the divine insight that comes from above. If we judge only on the basis of what we have been through, our view narrows and we easily become trapped in our wounds. That is why we must seek the leading of the Thought Adjuster in prayer, receive the illumination of the Spirit of Truth, and reinterpret our own experience in the light of revealed truth.

This principle applies just as well within a community. Just as those with long years of experience and those with fresh insight need one another, greater wisdom arises when people with different strengths take counsel together. The moment we believe we can know everything on our own, we move away from wisdom. If even the perfectors of Paradise co-operate, how much less can we be sufficient on our own!

Another passage about the Perfectors of Wisdom says that wherever they function, divine wisdom is at work (see 19:2.3). Yet even that perfect wisdom becomes more complete when paired with the wisdom of experience. Knowledge is knowing facts; wisdom is knowing how to use those facts for right purposes. One can possess a great deal of information and still act foolishly, and one can have learned little and yet live wisely. Wisdom is not gained by the head alone; it is engraved on the soul as we pass through life walking with God.

Today, let us seek both kinds of wisdom together. Let us treasure what we have learned from our own experience, yet lay it before God and examine it in a higher light. And let us listen to neighbors whose experience differs from ours. Where insight from above meets experience gathered from below, there, little by little, we become truly wise.
d040.pr: Take one decision you must make today, seek light from above in prayer, and then ask counsel of someone with experience.

msg: Many people have thought of the reason the Son of God came into this world in this way: to soften the heart of an angry Father and to change his attitude toward sinners. Today’s passage acknowledges that “⟦Q 20:5.2⟧on Urantia there is a widespread belief that the purpose of a Son’s bestowal is, in some manner, to influence the attitude of the Universal Father,⟦/Q⟧” and states plainly that “⟦Q 20:5.2⟧your enlightenment should indicate that this is not true.⟦/Q⟧” The love of the Universal Father has been unchanging from the beginning, and the bestowal of the Son was not meant to alter that love.

What, then, is the purpose of a bestowal? The passage explains that “⟦Q 20:5.2⟧the bestowals of the Avonal and the Michael Sons are a necessary part of the experiential process designed to make these Sons safe and sympathetic magistrates and rulers of the peoples and planets of time and space.⟦/Q⟧” In other words, the bestowal is not for the sake of the Father but for the Son’s own experience, and in the end for the creatures he cares for. Only a ruler who has lived the life of his creatures in person can truly understand and sympathize with them.

This teaching is in harmony with the picture of God that runs through the whole of The Urantia Book. The Universal Father is not one whose anger must be appeased but one who already and always loves his children. Jesus, too, showed the Father as a father waiting for the prodigal son (see Paper 169). The Father loved his children before they ever returned, and the life of the Son did not change that love; it revealed it. Even the cross was not a sacrifice to placate the Father’s wrath, but a revelation of love (see Paper 188).

This truth brings great freedom to our religious life. We do not need to strive to win God’s favor. Prayer is not a technique for persuading God, and worship is not a shield to ward off his displeasure. We come to the Father as children who are already loved. A religion born of fear makes people shrink, but a religion that knows love sets people free and makes them bold.

The passage also says that “⟦Q 20:5.2⟧all Magisterial Sons are motivated by this same spirit of service which so abundantly characterizes the primary Creator Sons and the Eternal Son of Paradise.⟦/Q⟧” The Sons of God come down to the lower worlds not to guard their status but to serve. To follow those Sons means to learn this very spirit of service. To go down to where others are in order to understand and sympathize with them: that is the way to live the spirit of bestowal in daily life.

What, then, were the sufferings and death that Jesus endured on Urantia? The Urantia Book teaches that they were not a transaction of atonement paying the debt of human sin. The Son did not die because God demanded blood; it was the ignorance and evil of men that drove him to his death. Yet even in the face of that death he showed love and forgiveness to the very end. So the cross became not a sign of the Father’s anger but a sign of how completely the Son loved, to the uttermost. And that love was the very love of the Father.

Today, let us lay down the fears that make us doubt the Father’s love. Even when we have stumbled, let us not imagine that he has turned his back on us, but return to the Father who is already waiting. And when someone is hard to understand, let us practice a small bestowal by standing in that person’s place. Those who believe in the Father’s unchanging love become channels through which that love flows on to their neighbors.
d041.pr: Today, instead of a prayer that tries to obtain something from God, offer a prayer of thanks that you are already loved.

d042.t: Divine Character Revealed in the Sons
msg: Today’s passage beautifully sums up how the Paradise Sons of God reveal the character of Deity to the universe. “⟦Q 20:10.3⟧In the Creator Sons the love of the Universal Father is blended with the mercy of the Eternal Son and is disclosed to the local universes in the creative power, loving ministry, and understanding sovereignty of the Michaels.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 20:10.3⟧In the Magisterial Sons the mercy of the Eternal Son, united with the ministry of the Infinite Spirit, is revealed to the evolutionary domains in the careers of these Avonals of judgment, service, and bestowal.⟦/Q⟧” And “⟦Q 20:10.3⟧in the Trinity Teacher Sons the love, mercy, and ministry of the three Paradise Deities are co-ordinated⟦/Q⟧” and “⟦Q 20:10.3⟧presented to the universes as living truth, divine goodness, and true spiritual beauty.⟦/Q⟧”

The key words of this paragraph are love, mercy, and ministry. Love is the nature of the Father, mercy is the nature of the Son, and ministry is the nature of the Spirit. These three are not separate from one another; they are combined in various ways within the different orders of Sons. The character of God is not a single monotone light but a rainbow in which many colors blend. Each order of Sons shows one color of that rainbow with special clarity, and together they reveal the fullness of Deity.

Michael, the father of our local universe of Nebadon, is the one among them who most deeply reveals the love of the Father. He possesses creative power, yet that power is always exercised as loving ministry and understanding sovereignty. His life as Jesus on Urantia showed how power yields to love. In him who healed the sick, embraced the outcast, and washed his disciples’ feet, we behold a divinity in which love, mercy, and ministry are blended into one.

The statement that the Daynal Teacher Sons present truth, goodness, and beauty is also worth pondering deeply. In The Urantia Book, truth, beauty, and goodness are the supreme spiritual values. God’s love, mercy, and ministry do not remain abstract doctrines; they come to us as truth we can know, beauty we can feel, and goodness we can do. To learn truth, to love beauty, and to do good are therefore all ways of participating in the character of God.

This teaching is also a call to our own character. As children of God, we too must hold love, mercy, and ministry together. Love without mercy easily becomes conditional; mercy without ministry remains mere sentiment; and ministry without love becomes dry duty. When the three blend together, our service begins to resemble the service of the Sons.

This paragraph also tells us that God, though one, comes to us in many ways. Some meet God in the majesty of the Creator, some in merciful forgiveness, and some in teaching and understanding. All of these encounters are different faces of the same divinity. So there is no need to look down on another person’s way of experiencing God just because it differs from mine. As the Paradise Sons each reveal Deity in their own way, so each person’s faith may be a unique path toward the same Father.

Today, let us reflect on which of these three is most lacking in our lives. If we love in our hearts but have not actually reached out a hand, let us add ministry; if we work hard but our hearts have grown dry, let us recover love; and if we have been severe before the faults of others, let us learn mercy. A day in which love, mercy, and ministry are in harmony becomes a small reflection of the revelation the Sons of God unfold throughout the universe.
d042.pr: Of love, mercy, and ministry, choose the one most lacking in you today and put it into practice through a concrete action.

d043.t: Virtue Is a Choice of Will
msg: Today’s passage shows the responsibility a Creator Son bears toward his creation. “⟦Q 21:3.14⟧If ever the authority or administration of a Creator Son is challenged, attacked, or jeopardized, he is eternally pledged to uphold, protect, defend, and if necessary retrieve his personal creation.⟦/Q⟧” The Creator does not abandon what he has made. That pledge is like the responsibility parents bear toward their children, but far deeper and more unchanging.

The passage then adds a surprising fact: “⟦Q 21:3.14⟧Such Sons can be troubled or harassed only by the creatures of their own making or by higher beings of their own choosing.⟦/Q⟧” Those who can most deeply wound a Creator Son are not enemies from outside but the very children he made in love. The Lucifer rebellion was just such an event (see Paper 53). Beings Michael had created challenged his rule, and as a result a number of worlds, Urantia among them, were long isolated.

The final sentence of the passage reveals the reason for all this: “⟦Q 21:3.14⟧Virtue is volitional with personality; righteousness is not automatic in freewill creatures.⟦/Q⟧” God did not make us puppets. The freedom to choose good is at the same time the freedom to choose evil. The fact that even celestial beings of high station could misuse this freedom shows that righteousness is never conferred automatically.

This truth makes us sober. Having lived a life of faith for many years, knowing a great deal, or holding a high position does not guarantee righteousness. Righteousness must be chosen anew each day. Yesterday’s good decision does not automatically secure today’s goodness. And so we must guard against pride and cultivate the humble habit of choosing the Father’s will afresh every day.

At the same time, this teaching reveals a great dignity. That our virtue is volitional means that when we choose the good, it truly becomes our own. Goodness that is coerced cannot be an achievement of personality, but goodness freely chosen endures as an eternal value. The Creator Son has given us that freedom, and he waits for us to return love to him through it. Only loyalty freely given truly delights him.

Here we may try to sense the heart of the Creator Son. How painful it must be to be challenged by the very children one has made! Yet even in the face of rebellion, Michael did not crush it at once by force. The Urantia Book explains that even the rebels were given ample time so that their choices might be fully revealed (see Paper 54). The patience that respects freedom was not weakness but deep love and wisdom. Because obedience obtained by force has no meaning, he endured long and waited for his children to return of their own accord. Thanks to that patience, the way of recovery still lies open for our world as well.

Today, let us watch carefully over our moments of choice. Each small act of honesty, each small kindness, each small act of patience is a choice of will, and those choices together become our character. And let us trust the Creator Son who has pledged never to forsake us. Even when we fall, he upholds and restores us. Our part is to respond to that love by freely choosing the good today as well.
d043.pr: Pause consciously before one small choice you face today, consider it carefully, and freely choose the way that accords with the Father’s will.

d044.t: The Way, the Truth, and the Life
msg: Today’s passage looks ahead to the eternal destiny of the Creator Sons. “⟦Q 21:6.4⟧Just as the Deity of the Supreme is actualizing by virtue of experiential service, so are the Creator Sons achieving the personal realization of the Paradise-divinity potentials bound up in their unfathomable natures.⟦/Q⟧” Quoting the words Jesus spoke on Urantia, “⟦Q 21:6.4⟧I am the way, the truth, and the life,⟦/Q⟧” the passage says, “⟦Q 21:6.4⟧we believe that in eternity the Michaels are literally destined to be ‘the way, the truth, and the life.’⟦/Q⟧”

This passage adds new depth to the words of Jesus. They are not merely the claim of a religious leader but a declaration about cosmic reality. Michael is “⟦Q 21:6.4⟧ever blazing the path for all universe personalities as it leads from supreme divinity through ultimate absonity to eternal deity finality.⟦/Q⟧” He is not only the one who teaches us the way; he himself is the way. To live following his life is to walk the path that leads to the Father.

It is also significant that the passage emphasizes experiential service. As the Supreme Being is actualized through experience, so the Creator Sons realize their divine potentials through bestowal and service. The life Michael lived on Urantia was not only something he did for us; it was also the process by which he himself was being perfected as universe sovereign (see Papers 119 and 120). That even a Son of God grows through experience tells us that growth is a fundamental principle of the universe.

What, then, does it mean for us that he is the way, the truth, and the life? The way is the example that shows us how we ought to live. The truth is the true knowledge of God and of ourselves. The life is the eternal life that grows within us as we follow that way and that truth. The religion of Jesus is, before it is believing doctrines about him, walking together the path he walked and making his faith our own (see Paper 196).

A way has meaning only when it is walked. It is of no use to pore over a map and say we know the road. In the same way, if we confess Jesus as the way but do not practice his love and service, our confession becomes hollow. The Spirit of Truth he has sent us lights that way within our hearts and leads us, step by step each day, toward the Father. We need only respond to that leading and take the step.

The passage implies that the destiny of the Michaels has not yet been fully revealed. Unfathomable divinity potentials are bound up in their natures, and these will go on unfolding throughout eternity. This means that our Lord is not a static being already finished, but a living personality who keeps growing and expanding along with the universe. So it is with us who follow him. Our spiritual career does not end at any one point; it is an endless adventure that leads through the mansion worlds, the local universe, and Havona to Paradise, and on beyond.

Today, let us follow him who is the way, the truth, and the life in the concrete circumstances of our lives. Before a decision, let us ask what Jesus would have done; in confusion, let us seek the truth; and in weary moments, let us rely on the strength of life he gives. The way he lights leads us from today’s small obedience all the way to eternal Paradise. On that way we are never alone.
d044.pr: Before one decision today, ask what Jesus would have done, and take one step following that answer.

msg: Today’s passage tells us who the Mighty Messengers are. “⟦Q 22:2.3⟧Every ascendant mortal of insurrectionary experience who functions loyally in the face of rebellion is eventually destined to become a Mighty Messenger of the superuniverse service.⟦/Q⟧” But the passage goes a step further: “⟦Q 22:2.3⟧Likewise is any ascendant creature who effectively prevents such upheavals of error, evil, or sin; for action designed to prevent rebellion or to effect higher types of loyalty in a universe crisis is regarded as of even greater value than loyalty in the face of actual rebellion.⟦/Q⟧”

These words overturn our common sense. We usually remember as heroes those who held fast to the end in a great crisis. The one who puts out a fire after it breaks out is praised, but the one who watched carefully so that no fire broke out is seldom remembered. The universe, however, judges values differently. Loyalty that endures a crisis is precious, but loyalty that wisely prevents a crisis from ever arising is more precious still. The unseen loyalty of prevention is the highest loyalty of all.

Urantia is a world deeply affected by the Lucifer rebellion (see Paper 53). In that rebellion, when the Planetary Prince Caligastia joined the rebels, loyal ones such as Van and his human associate Amadon stood firm at their posts. Born into a world of rebellion, we are in this sense beings with a special opportunity. In a world full of confusion and doubt, keeping faith is itself an experience of loyalty. The loyalty shown by Van and Amadon was the courage to stand on the right side even when everything seemed to be collapsing (see Paper 67). Yet their loyalty shines all the brighter because, for long ages afterward, they taught and cared for those who remained and guarded the world against the spread of still greater confusion.

Today’s passage, however, points us to an even higher loyalty. It is the loyalty that tends things in advance so that error and evil do not grow up around us. Resolving a small distrust at home through conversation before it spreads into a deep wound; stopping gossip in a community before it grows into division; uprooting a small resentment in our own hearts with forgiveness before it becomes a bitter root: all of these are the loyalty that prevents rebellion.

Such loyalty requires wisdom, love, and watchfulness. Preventing problems in advance demands more delicate attention than cleaning up after they erupt. It requires the ability to read people’s hearts, to notice small signals, and to correct gently when needed. The reason the Mighty Messengers become such sympathetic ministers is that they learned this sensitivity through the experience of rebellion.

This teaching also awakens us to the value of ordinary days. A peaceful day on which nothing happened may not have come about by itself. Someone’s unseen patience, consideration, and prayer may have kept that peace. The universe never forgets such hidden loyalty, and it values it all the more highly. The small peace we keep is one form of cosmic loyalty.

Today, let us look for the small seeds of error and discord trying to grow around us. And let us deal with them in love and wisdom before they grow large. It is all right not to become a conspicuous hero. It is the quiet loyalty that prevents rebellion that helps us grow into children the Father can trust.
d045.pr: Today, find one small resentment or misunderstanding growing in your heart or relationships, and resolve it before it grows.

msg: Today’s passage is an astonishing promise that a Mighty Messenger speaks directly to the readers of Urantia: “⟦Q 22:4.7⟧You mortals who read this message may yourselves ascend to Paradise, attain the Trinity embrace, and in remote future ages be attached to the service of the Ancients of Days in one of the seven superuniverses, and sometime be assigned to enlarge the revelation of truth to some evolving inhabited planet, even as I am now functioning on Urantia.⟦/Q⟧” The one who delivers the revelation is telling those who read it, “You can become as I am.”

Let us weigh these words. The Mighty Messengers were once mortals born on evolutionary worlds, as we are. They kept their loyalty amid the trials of rebellion, passed through a long ascending career to reach Paradise, and, embraced by the Trinity, were entrusted with high service in the superuniverse. Their today may become our tomorrow. That many of the exalted beings of heaven began from the same starting point as we did gives us great hope.

The universe portrayed in The Urantia Book is not a caste society in which the high and the lowly are forever divided. A way lies open for even the lowliest will creature to ascend to Paradise. That way begins with the mandate of the Universal Father, the invitation, “⟦Q 1:0.3⟧Be you perfect, even as I am perfect⟦/Q⟧” (see Paper 1). The Thought Adjuster indwells us precisely so that this wondrous destiny may be fulfilled. We begin from an animal origin, but we were made to advance toward a divine destiny.

This promise also joins into one the revelation we now receive and the revelation we may someday share. Today we stand in the place of those who receive revelation, but in the distant future we may stand in the place of those who deliver it. If so, the way we learn truth now is very important. We are not merely accumulating knowledge; we are being prepared to become beings who can someday bring truth to our brothers on other worlds. Today’s study and meditation are training for eternal service.

At the same time, this promise calls us to service here and now. If we are destined to bring truth in the far future, we should be able to share truth with the people beside us now. It need not be a grand sermon. A sincere life, a single warm word, and steady trust in God are already ways of conveying truth. The work of enlarging revelation can already begin in our daily lives.

When we feel insignificant, let us remember these words. An exalted being of heaven is telling us that we, too, may become so. This is not pleasant consolation but a promise grounded in the actual plan of the universe. Our possibilities are far greater than the weakness we now feel. The Universal Father already sees those possibilities in us. That hope does not make us proud; rather, it makes us humble, for that high destiny is not our own merit but the Father’s gift.

Today, let us see ourselves as beings with an eternal destiny. And let us carry out today’s small tasks with care, as befits that destiny. The road to Paradise begins not in the far-off future but with the step we take today. If we are someday to bring truth to other worlds, we must first live the truth here and now.
d046.pr: Today, warmly share with someone, in word or deed, one truth you have learned.

msg: Why is there so much confusion and suffering in this world? If God truly cares for us, why does he not make the world a paradise? Today’s passage answers this ancient question head-on. “⟦Q 23:2.12⟧The confusion and turmoil of Urantia do not signify that the Paradise Rulers lack either interest or ability to manage affairs differently. The Creators are possessed of full power to make Urantia a veritable paradise, but such an Eden would not contribute to the development of those strong, noble, and experienced characters⟦/Q⟧” within us.

The passage explains this through the image of a forge. The Gods are “⟦Q 23:2.12⟧so surely forging out on your world between the anvils of necessity and the hammers of anguish⟦/Q⟧” our characters. Just as a blacksmith must heat iron in the fire and pound it with a hammer on the anvil to make a sturdy tool, so our characters are tempered under trial and pressure. Where there is no difficulty at all, neither courage nor patience, neither trust nor compassion, can grow. Suffering is not the goal, but it can become a tool for shaping character.

Elsewhere The Urantia Book explains in detail the value of the difficulties of the evolutionary worlds (see Paper 3, section 5). Only amid uncertainty does faith grow; only amid disappointment is hope tempered; amid injustice the love of justice is born; and only through suffering neighbors does unselfish service become possible. These experiences, absent from perfect Havona, are unique opportunities given only to the mortals of the evolutionary worlds. Our trials are not mistakes of the universe but part of the divine plan.

This does not mean, however, that we should make light of suffering. Nor does it mean that God sends us suffering. Much suffering is the result of human ignorance and evil, and of rebellion. But whatever suffering comes, it need not end in breaking us; it can become the thing that tempers us. That is the promise of the passage. The meaning of suffering lies not in suffering itself but in how we respond to it.

The passage says, “⟦Q 23:2.12⟧Your anxieties and sorrows, your trials and disappointments, are just as much a part of the divine plan on your sphere as are the exquisite perfection and infinite adaptation of all things to their supreme purpose on the worlds of the central and perfect universe.⟦/Q⟧” This is an astonishing comfort. Just as the perfection of Havona is God’s plan, so the imperfection of our world also lies within God’s plan. We do not live in an abandoned world, but in a world being tempered under the hand of the divine smith.

So when trials come, we can remember two things. One is that God still cares and is still able; the other is that this trial can shape us into stronger and nobler persons. With these two convictions, we need not despair even in suffering, and we can choose growth instead of resentment. Each stroke of the hammer brings us closer to the likeness of the Father.

Let us call to mind one difficulty we are going through today. And let us set it upon the anvil of the divine forge. What character might grow in me through this difficulty? Patience? Courage? Or a heart that understands the pain of others? As we bear this day while seeking that character, our suffering is transformed into eternal value.
d047.pr: Write down one difficulty you are facing now, and name one quality of character that can grow in you through it.

msg: Today’s passage introduces one beautiful ministry of the Solitary Messengers. “⟦Q 23:4.1⟧The Solitary Messengers seem to be personality co-ordinators for all types of spirit beings. Their ministry helps to make all the personalities of the far-flung spiritual world akin.⟦/Q⟧” They contribute much to the development, in all spirit beings, of “⟦Q 23:4.1⟧a consciousness of group identity,⟦/Q⟧” and they “⟦Q 23:4.1⟧foster the ability of such beings to understand and fraternize with all other types and orders, however dissimilar.⟦/Q⟧”

The Solitary Messengers are, as their name says, beings who travel and work alone. For technical reasons they must always travel and function alone (see 23:1.9). It is a profound paradox that these very solitary beings should be the ones who join all other beings together. They do not remain shut up in loneliness; rather, they become the bond that ties all the personalities of the universe into one family. They show us that solitude can be not isolation but a service of connection.

The universe portrayed in The Urantia Book is filled with an astonishing diversity of beings. There are seraphim and cherubim, Melchizedeks and midwayers, finaliters and Havona natives, orders beyond counting. They differ in origin, in nature, and in function. Yet the universe does not leave this diversity in confusion. Through the ministry of co-ordinators such as the Solitary Messengers, different beings come to understand one another, to fellowship, and to become one family. Unity in diversity: this is a principle of the universe.

Our world needs this principle just as much. Humanity differs in race, language, religion, and culture. Those differences have often been the cause of misunderstanding, conflict, and war. Yet difference itself is not the problem. The problem is a lack of the ability to understand and fraternize with one another. Those who know the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man can look beyond differences and see others as kin.

We, too, can become little Solitary Messengers. At home, at work, and in our communities of faith, we can be people who build bridges between those who differ: between generations, between people of differing views, helping them to understand one another. To do this, I must first have a heart that seeks to understand others deeply. When we put understanding before judgment and listening before insisting, we become people who bind others together.

At times we too pass through seasons of solitude. There are times when we feel the loneliness of thinking that no one understands us. But as the Solitary Messengers show, time alone can become preparation for the service of connecting others. Those who know loneliness deeply are better able to recognize the loneliness of others and to lead them into community. Solitude becomes a time of deep communion with God, and that communion flows out again as love toward our neighbors.

Today, let us think of people around us who do not understand one another. And let us look for ways to build a small bridge between them. Gently conveying one person’s point of view to another, inviting someone left out into the conversation: such small acts are ways of joining in the holy ministry that makes the universe a family.
d048.pr: In conversation today, find one person who is being left out and naturally invite him or her in.

msg: Today’s passage introduces unique beings called the Census Directors. “⟦Q 24:2.8⟧Census Directors register the existence of a new will creature when the first act of will is performed; they indicate the death of a will creature when the last act of will takes place.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 24:2.8⟧The partial emergence of will observed in the reactions of certain of the higher animals does not belong to the domain of the Census Directors.⟦/Q⟧” “⟦Q 24:2.8⟧They keep count of nothing but bona fide will creatures, and they are responsive to nothing but will function.⟦/Q⟧” Even the author of the passage confesses, “⟦Q 24:2.8⟧Exactly how they register the function of will, we do not know.⟦/Q⟧”

This short paragraph shows what the universe regards as most important. The census of the universe is not based on the birth of a body or the cessation of breath. Its criterion is will. The moment a being first exercises a will capable of moral choice, he is registered in the universe as a will creature. In the eyes of the universe, what makes a person a person is not the body but the capacity of personality to choose for itself.

The Urantia Book explains in many places how important this moment is in the spiritual career of a human being. When a child makes his first moral decision, usually a little before the age of six, a Thought Adjuster comes to indwell that child (see Paper 108). The awakening of will becomes the door through which the divine spirit arrives. The universe records our first act of will because from that moment we become beings who can begin an eternal career together with God.

This teaching awakens us to the dignity of the will. The choices we make each day are not mere habits or reactions. They are acts of personality to which the universe pays attention. Whether we choose good or evil, we are shaping who we are. Animals follow instinct, but will creatures choose. This very capacity for choice is the sign that we are children of the Father.

We must therefore treat the will with care. To hand our will over to others, to let it be seized by addiction and bad habits, or to choose nothing at all out of fear, is to neglect the most precious gift we have been given. When, on the contrary, we choose to do God’s will, our will finds its highest use. Jesus taught that aligning our will with the Father’s will is true freedom.

It is also worth pondering that the passage records the last act of will as death. The will may stop functioning even before physical death comes. To be alive, then, is not merely to breathe, but to live choosing with a will. Those who renew their will toward God each day are truly alive. May each of our days be a day of awakened will. The fact that the universe has recorded our first act of will tells us that none of our choices is ever trivial. Our personality is a responsible being whose name stands in the registry of the universe. Those who remember that dignity do not easily give up on themselves.

Today, let us be conscious of the choices we make. Let us make choices not that we let slip by unthinkingly, but that we make with an awakened will. And let us offer a prayer aligning that will with the Father’s will. The confession “⟦Q 111:5.6⟧It is my will that your will be done⟦/Q⟧” is the highest worship a will creature can offer.
d049.pr: Today, stop one thing you have been doing without thinking, and choose it again with an awakened will.
